newsitem.title: PERU: Peru cenbank says Q1 primary surplus 830 mln soles.
newsitem.headline: Peru cenbank says Q1 primary surplus 830 mln soles.

text.p: The Central Reserve Bank of Peru said Tuesday the government's primary surplus at the end of the first quarter this year was 830 million soles ($313 million), compared with 351 million soles at the end of the first quarter in 1996.
The central bank defines the primary surplus as the difference between the government's spending -- excluding interest payments on debt -- and its income.
The government has agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on a goal of increasing its primary surplus to 1.3 percent of GDP in 1997 from 1.1 percent last year.
But the bank did not announce the result of its first quarter calculations measuring the surplus as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP).
